newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICAN OIL, CHEMISTRY DEADLOCK MEDIATION FAILS.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICAN OIL, CHEMISTRY DEADLOCK MEDIATION FAILS.

text.p: Efforts to resolve the deadlock over wage increases and working conditions between South Africa's strategic oil and chemicals industries and workers have failed, employers said on Friday.

Oil industry labour spokesman Simon Drysdale told Reuters that two, two-day efforts by the Council for Conciliation, Mediation and Arbitration (CCMA) to resolve the dispute had not been able to resolve differences between employers and the Chemical Workers Industrial Union (CWIU).
"It looks like the whole chemical industry will be affected, not only the oil industry," Drysdale said.
In terms of new labour legislation, the CCMA is expected to issue a certificate soon stating that the parties could not reach agreement.
"Then each party will exercise its rights," Drysdale said.
This could lead to strikes or overtime bans.

The wage talks deadlocked last month with employers offering a 9.5 percent wage increase and workers demanding 14.5 percent plus a 40 hour working week and six months maternity leave with four months paid in full.

By the time the mediation failed on Friday, workers were demanding a 13 percent wage increase and employers were offering 10 percent. Employers were still offering a 42 hour working week and six months maternity leave with four months paid at 33 percent.
Drysdale said that the CWIU had informed employers that it would take part in the one hour strike planned by the Congress of South African Trade Unions on August 4.
He did not expect this to have any major effect on the oil industry as few workers had participated in the last such strike in protest against the proposed Basic Conditions of Employment Bill.
